title: Purely inseparable subfields of a one-variable function field are power subfields
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], [def-pc-field-characteristic], and let $k\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be fields [def-pc-field-extension]. Assume that $E/k$ and $L/k$ are finitely generated as fields (each is generated over $k$ by finitely many elements) and have transcendence degree one [def-kun-transcendence-degree], and that $L/E$ is finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Then there exists an integer $r\geq0$ such that
$$[L:E]=p^r\qquad\text{and}\qquad E=L^{p^r}:=\{x^{p^r}:x\in L\},$$
where degree means vector-space dimension [def-pc-field-tower] and the equality is an equality of subfields of $L$, with their given inclusions.

source.place: Tags 0CCX (lemma-purely-inseparable) and 0CCY (lemma-inseparable-deg-p-smooth), field-theoretic content of their proofs, specialized to algebraically closed k: degree-p tower and equality with the power subfield.

proof.text: The positive characteristic $p$ is prime: a factorization $p=ab$ with $1<a,b<p$ would give nonzero elements $a\cdot1,b\cdot1$ with zero product in $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower] to $L/E$. Write its tower as $E=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_r=L$, where $F_i=F_{i-1}(\alpha_i)$, $\alpha_i^p\in F_{i-1}$ and $[F_i:F_{i-1}]=p$. Every $F_i/k$ is finitely generated: append $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_i$ to the given finite generators of $E/k$. Each $F_i/E$ is algebraic directly from pure inseparability of $L/E$: for $x\in F_i\subseteq L$ some $x^{p^m}$ belongs to $E$, so $x$ satisfies the nonzero polynomial $X^{p^m}-x^{p^m}\in E[X]$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. By [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower], $\operatorname{trdeg}_k F_i=\operatorname{trdeg}_k E=1$.

source.place: Tag 0CCX (lemma-purely-inseparable), reduction to the degree-p tower of fields.tex Tag 09HI (lemma-finite-purely-inseparable); fields.tex Tags 09G9 and 030H for degrees and transcendence degrees.

proof.text: For each $i$, [lem-trf-algclosed-curve-model] applies to the finitely generated extension $F_i/k$ of transcendence degree one, since $k$ is algebraically closed. Choose its smooth proper integral curve $C_i$ and $k$-isomorphism $k(C_i)\cong F_i$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-curve-function-field-p-basis] to $C_i$. Its conclusion $[k(C_i):k(C_i)^p]=p$ gives $[F_i:F_i^p]=p$: if $\theta:k(C_i)\to F_i$ is the chosen isomorphism, then $\theta(x^p)=\theta(x)^p$, so it maps the power subfields onto one another and sends the stated basis to a basis. Indeed applying $\theta$ or $\theta^{-1}$ to a linear combination proves respectively spanning and linear independence over these subfields.

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (theorem-curves-rational-maps), existence of curve models, and Tag 0BY3 (lemma-nonsingular-model-smooth); Tag 0CCY (lemma-inseparable-deg-p-smooth), second proof paragraph, p-basis computation (more-algebra.tex Tag 07P2).

proof.text: For $1\leq i\leq r$, write any $x\in F_i=F_{i-1}(\alpha_i)$ as $P(\alpha_i)/Q(\alpha_i)$ with $P,Q\in F_{i-1}[X]$ and $Q(\alpha_i)\ne0$. In characteristic $p$, taking $p$th powers raises each coefficient to its $p$th power and replaces $\alpha_i$ by $\alpha_i^p\in F_{i-1}$. Thus $x^p\in F_{i-1}$, proving $F_i^p\subseteq F_{i-1}$. The set $F_i^p$ is a subfield, since $p$th powers commute with sums, products and inverses in characteristic $p$. The space $F_{i-1}$ over $F_i^p$ is finite-dimensional: any linearly independent family in it is also independent in $F_i$, so has at most $p$ elements by Step 2. The other degree $[F_i:F_{i-1}]=p$ is supplied by Step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] to $F_i/F_{i-1}/F_i^p$. Steps 1 and 2 give $p=p[F_{i-1}:F_i^p]$, so $[F_{i-1}:F_i^p]=1$. A one-dimensional field extension equals its base field since the nonzero vector $1$ spans it. Hence $F_{i-1}=F_i^p$ as actual subfields of $L$.

source.place: Tag 0CCY (lemma-inseparable-deg-p-smooth), final reasons-of-degree comparison, with containment written using the degree-p root presentation of fields.tex Tag 09HI; degree multiplication is fields.tex Tag 09G9.

proof.text: Starting with $F_r=L$, induction down the tower now gives $F_{r-j}=L^{p^j}$ for $0\leq j\leq r$: the base is $F_r=L=L^{p^0}$ and the step uses $F_{r-j-1}=F_{r-j}^p$ and $(L^{p^j})^p=L^{p^{j+1}}$, the equality of the sets of powers. Thus $E=F_0=L^{p^r}$. Repeated application of [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] to the tower of Step 1 gives $[L:E]=\prod_{i=1}^r[F_i:F_{i-1}]=p^r$. For $r=0$ the tower is empty, $E=L$, and the formula is $[L:L]=1=p^0$.
